Project VektaKillzone HD: Unofficial PC Port (static recompilation)

A native Linux and Windows x64 port of the 2011 PS3 remaster of the first Killzone, made by static recompilation: the game's PowerPC and SPU code is translated to C++ ahead of time and compiled into a PC program on your machine; graphics go through Vulkan. No emulator runs at play time.

Status: Partly playable

You need your own copy of the game. This project ships no game code, data, assets or keys.

See the statusSource on GitHub

The same pins will go into the Windows installer.

0.1.0

31 Oct 2026 · pre-release

  • AddedThe game's own MLAA anti-aliasing, reimplemented as a GPU compute pass equal to the SPU code (patches 2035 to 2037, KZ_MLAA=gpu|spu|off); the first frame no longer waits for the driver to compile it.
  • AddedNVIDIA Reflex (Off, On, On + Boost) on the PC page, through VK_NV_low_latency2 (patch 2038).
  • AddedIn-game key capture for remapping screens (patch 4011).
  • Addedtools/wine-test.sh runs the Windows build under Wine or Proton for a minute and says whether it held its frame rate; it passed at 144 fps under both on the maintainer's machine.
  • Addedtools/mlaa_harness and tools/mlaa_probe: the lifted MLAA jobs run outside the game, test patterns and checks.
  • AddedReleases: VERSION holds the one version string; tools/release/bump_version.py moves it everywhere and turns this section into the release's entry; a pushed tag builds a reproducible source archive (the tree with ps3recomp at its pinned commit) and opens a draft pre-release with notes from this file and SHA-256 sums (docs/RELEASE-CRITERIA.md).
  • ChangedThe project page is generated whole from the repository (the feature table, the screenshots, this changelog, the requirements and the patch series) and laid out like the Killzone 2 and Killzone 3 ports' pages; docs/FEATURES.md gains a section on the port itself (builds, frame rate, installer).
  • Fixedtools/release/bump_version.py leaves an empty ## [Unreleased] above the entry it releases, and an empty entry is not news on the project page.
  • Fixedtools/ps3recomp-patched.sh also works in an unpacked source archive, where there is no git checkout.
  • FixedAn SPU write into a GPU-mapped range that overlaps one already unmapped is seen as GPU-mapped again (patch 2039), and the SPU poison-write diagnostic works with SPU_POISON_DMA_WATCH (patch 1019); both found by ps3recomp's own tests, which now run on the patched tree in CI (patch 0004).
  • FixedAn SPU that reserves a line while another SPU's plain write to it is being copied now loses the reservation at once, not at the next 10 ms poll (patch 1020).

The whole changelog >

About the port

how it works · ps3recomp v0.18.0 · 102 patches

The port is built on ps3recomp (MIT), pinned at v0.18.0 with 102 patches of this project: the PPU code and the game's SPU programs are lifted to C++, the PS3 system libraries the game calls are reimplemented, and the game's RSX command stream is replayed on Vulkan. It builds natively on Linux, and on Linux for Windows; the Windows build is tested under Wine, Proton and on Windows.

It follows Project Helghast and Project Pyrrhus, the same method applied to Killzone 3 and Killzone 2, and reuses their general runtime work. About 65 % of Killzone HD is done, and 41 % of the whole trilogy plan; what comes next: the roadmap.

Full status

Install

v0.1.0 pre-release

31 Oct 2026 · partly playable · source for Linux x64

Download v0.1.0All releases

The release page has project-vekta-0.1.0-source.tar.gz (this version's tree with ps3recomp at its pinned commit) with a .sha256 file, and SHA256SUMS: check your download against them. There is no installer yet: the archive builds the port as below.

The build checks your own Killzone HD files, translates the game's code and builds it on your machine. Nothing of the game is shipped or downloaded, and nothing is written into your game files. What each input must contain: Getting your files.

git clone --recurse-submodules \
  https://github.com/gustavomorinaga/project-vekta
cd project-vekta
tools/check-game-files.py
tools/ps3recomp-patched.sh
tools/lift.sh
tools/setup-vfs.sh
tools/build.sh
tools/play.sh

The steps, and the Windows build: building.

What goes online

Nothing. The port, its scripts and the build make no network connection of their own; the only downloads are the ones you start (this repository, its ps3recomp submodule, your system's packages). Where your saves and settings go: the README.

Viewing this website loads the Fira Sans Condensed font from Google Fonts, which sees your visit; the repository, the build and the game do not.

Requirements

What you need

Your own Killzone HD (NPUA80856) from the Killzone Trilogy disc, installed, with its decrypted EBOOT and data archive, and the decrypted libsre and dev_flash of PS3 system software 4.93: GETTING-FILES.md. No PlayStation Network account is used.

Hardware to play

MinimumTested
Operating systemLinux x64; Windows x64 (other Windows versions and machines not tried)CachyOS (Linux x64); the maintainer's Windows install for the cross-built exe; Wine and Proton (GE-Proton 11, proton-cachyos)
CPUx86-64 with AVX2 (x86-64-v3, Intel Haswell or AMD Zen and newer), the default build target; KZ_MARCH="" builds for any x86-64, untestedthe maintainer's desktop CPU with AVX-512 (KZ_MARCH=x86-64-v4)
GPUa Vulkan GPU and driver; other vendors not tried yetNVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Ti, driver 615
Memorybuilding: several GB for the lifted code (use fewer jobs on small machines); playing: not measured
Diskabout 4 GB for the game files, plus the build (work/), a few GB

Details: requirements.md. The tested column is the maintainer's machine; reports from other hardware are welcome.

Notice and creditsLicence (MIT)Project HelghastProject Pyrrhus

Killzone and Killzone HD are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment. This project is not affiliated with or endorsed by Sony Interactive Entertainment or Guerrilla Games; the names are used only to say which game the port runs. "Vekta" is the name of the game's own colony world. No game content is distributed: no disc or PSN files, no decrypted or translated game code, no assets, no firmware and no keys. Players supply their own copy of the game; the game's code is translated and compiled on the player's own machine from their own files.

The port's own code, tools and documentation are MIT. Third-party components and credits: NOTICE.md.
